summary: The candidate is mathematically correct. Affine equivariance gives a bijection on legal exact-minorant cap choices and preserves balance, negativity, support-minimality, descendant fibers, centerpoint weights, and core emptiness, so arbitrary adaptive normalizations do not alter the argument. In one continuous dimension every support-minimal negative balanced certificate has two opposite nonzero normals. Exactness at the center base forces the center cap sections independently of the minorant slopes; their weighted Minkowski interval has length at least 1/4 and shift at most epsilon, while each outer descendant fiber remains inside the original outer interval and stays positive by the accepted predecessor fact. The resulting affine rescaling therefore enlarges the outer-fiber radius by at most a factor of 8. Iteration from C_L keeps the radius below 1/8 through step L, which preserves the unique centerpoint, empty core, and three-point positive lattice support for every adaptive legal chain. The final mixed-depth and total-mass computations are also valid.
